prize_parts.citation: For the discovery that liquid-liquid phase separation, driven by multivalent molecular interactions, is a physical-chemical principle by which cells organise their contents into membraneless compartments

statement.case_for: After reading the whole exchange I keep B003 as my single-part position, but I now word the citation around what I think is secure: biomolecular condensates as liquid-like phases with measurable surface tension, fusion and dripping (Brangwynne, Hyman 2009), and sharp, concentration-dependent phase transitions of multivalent molecules whose onset follows the valency and affinity of the interacting modules (Rosen and colleagues, 2012). Those two results are thermodynamic statements that have been reproduced in vitro and in several cell systems, and they do not depend on any specific condensate being phase-separated at endogenous concentrations. The concept changed how physiology, signalling, stress response and neurodegeneration are framed, and it is a case where physical chemistry, not a new reagent, supplied the idea. The citation names the principle and not a list of biological claims, which answers the chair's first question.
statement.case_against: The reservations raised in round 1 are real and I do not dismiss them. Several in vivo claims for particular condensates fail when concentrations are not physiological, the boundary between demixing and other assemblies is blurred, and there is no therapeutic payoff yet, so a prize is a bet that the principle outlives the contested examples. Attribution remains uncomfortable: Pappu and Mittag's sequence-grammar work is the most quantitative part of the field and is left out of a three-name trio, and an honest reading is that Rosen over Pappu is a judgment on priority and on who showed sufficiency first, not an obvious call. B068 is the better choice on molecular definition and design, but it has an unresolved split between PROTAC and glue lineages and no approved PROTAC drug.

responses.point: Heiner agreed on the origin and on Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen but asked me to say plainly which results hold up and whether the core can be separated from contested in vivo claims.
responses.response: What I consider secure is limited. First, P-granule-type assemblies behave as liquids by the usual operational tests: they fuse, wet, drip under shear, and their components exchange rapidly, which fixes a surface tension and a viscosity. Second, purified multivalent proteins and their ligands undergo a sharp transition at a threshold concentration that depends on valency and affinity, and this is reproduced in many in vitro systems. Third, these two results carry no claim about the physiological state of any given condensate. What does not hold up is the broad inference that a visible punctum in an overexpressing cell is a phase-separated body. I would write the citation for the principle and the demonstrated physical behaviour, so the contested claims fall outside it. This is how I would make the case timely; if the committee wants more than that, I accept that my position weakens.

responses.point: Peter ranks B003 fourth, says fifteen years does not make it mature, and wants the physical principle separated from the biological claims.
responses.response: I accept that duration of work is not a measure of maturity and I should not have leaned on it. The better test is whether the claim being credited has stood against independent reanalysis, and the in vitro thermodynamics has, while the in vivo generality has not. That is why I have narrowed the citation. Your point on nitrogenase also helps me: we both accept a prize that credits a well-supported structural and physical core while leaving the full mechanism open, and I think the same standard should be applied to B003 and to B009. I remain unconvinced that unresolved intermediates are less damaging to a nitrogenase citation than unresolved in vivo generality is to mine, but the two are comparable and I see no basis for calling one premature and not the other.

responses.point: Daniel argues that degrader mechanisms are molecularly defined with ternary-complex structures and that B003 should be the strongest alternative only if the committee wants a mature physical-chemistry prize.
responses.response: I agree that ternary-complex structures and direct measurement of degradation give B068 a more defined mechanism, and that is why it is my first alternative. My difficulty is the one Andrei states and you partly share: the PROTAC trio omits the cereblon glue lineage that has the approved drugs, and your own offer to narrow the citation to the PROTAC concept shows the three-name cap is doing real work. In your reply to my question you did not say how Ciulli should be justified against Handa. If the committee decides B068 as one prize, I would want Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli only with a citation limited to heterobifunctional degraders and an explicit statement that the glue lineage is not credited. I think that is less clean than the B003 trio.

responses.point: Andrei supports B068 but says a PROTAC-only trio leaves out the part of the field with the most patient benefit, and that any split of three names would look arbitrary if the lineages are not separated.
responses.response: This is the sharpest objection to B068 in the record, and I find it more serious than the in vivo objection to B003, since it concerns attribution and not only timing. If glue and PROTAC are one scientific lineage, three names cannot cover it; if they are two, they are two parts, and two parts would already use the full cap of three people only with a weakened case for each. For that reason I would not move to B068 in a single-part form this year unless the committee settles the lineage question. I would value your view on whether Handa or Sakamoto is the more defensible third name if the committee takes only the PROTAC concept.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a citation limited to the in vitro and cellular physical principle, and treats contested in vivo condensate claims as outside the prize
Whether Rosen or Pappu (or Mittag) is the right third laureate, given sequence-encoded phase behaviour
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one lineage or two, and whether B068 can then be credited fairly within three names
Whether the committee prefers reproducibility and clean attribution (B009, B004) over conceptual reach when no ballot has a majority
Whether recent prizes in related areas leave room for B025 or B032 in a later year
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited candidate. I share a Lund affiliation with Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, but no shortlisted candidate is linked to Lund in the statements. My membrane, lipid and amyloid research is close to phase separation and to lipid nanoparticle science (B025), and Daniel Aili's peptide self-assembly work overlaps with mine. I have no personal or institutional tie to any credited person and do not regard this as a recusal issue.
